findings.claim: A promised heading quoted inside a fence is not the section it names.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: slice(0,3) collapsed fence length, so a three-backtick line closed a four-backtick opener; a draft whose entire body sat inside a four-backtick fence with one nested example passed as 'shape TEMPLATE'. Under CommonMark it is one code block with zero headings.

findings.claim: MIGRATION named only tightenings; the cure was one re-run of totem spec.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a twenty-tilde divider went main pass -> branch block 'is missing heading <h>' for a heading present verbatim; a four-space-indented fence line and a backtick opener with a backtick info string opened fences CommonMark does not.

findings.claim: Only the strict TEMPLATE arm moves; the DOCUMENT shape is unchanged.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED with promptSource override: a fenced YAML document with '# Problem' comments went main pass -> branch 'has no heading with a body'; the record arm shares the predicate and its cure is editing the record.

findings.claim: Scope is the reader only; no doc update owed.
findings.counterexample: The TEMPLATE and DOCUMENT rows stated rules with no fence or bare-hash clause; the immediately preceding reader change (mmnto-ai/totem#2737) updated this file in lockstep.

findings.claim: A line inside a fence IS body when non-blank.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: bareHashes was applied before the in-fence check, so a fence holding '####' read as empty.

findings.claim: 'a heading that appears fenced first and real later is found at the real line'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: the draft passed on origin/main too (the fenced copy matched); the discriminating shape (exact fenced, tolerant real) yields '· tolerated' only on the branch.

findings.claim: Nine cases pin the fence state.
findings.counterexample: Unpinned: unequal fence lengths, indented fence, tilde rule, DOCUMENT arm under fences, '####' inside a fence, the tolerated discriminator, seven hashes.

findings.claim: A written code block is a written section, so fenced lines are body.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a section whose only content was a fence containing the next promised heading passed with zero authored words.

findings.claim: isBody excluded only an EXACT promised heading inside a fence while the matcher treats the parenthetical-stripped spelling as the same heading.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a section whose only content was a fence containing '### Execution Flow' (tolerant spelling) passed; the exact spelling blocked.

findings.claim: The indent-4 pin pinned the indent rule.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: the draft passed identically on origin/main, fold 1 and fold 2 — bodied by a plain indented line under any fence semantics; the discriminating draft (indented opener, skeleton after, no closer) fails on fold 1 only.

findings.claim: MIGRATION names only the divider class; a fence closed by repeating the info string is a new block class with the wrong stated cure.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: '```mermaid / A --> B / ```mermaid' went main pass, fold 1 pass, fold 2 block; a re-run of totem spec may reproduce it; the cure is a bare closing fence.

findings.claim: fencedCopyOf compared trimEnd()'d lines, so an indented fenced skeleton escaped the hint and an indented fenced promised heading counted as body.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: the skeleton quoted inside a fence with two-space indentation blocked with the bare 'is missing heading' and no fence hint; '  ### Execution Flow (structural constraint)' inside a fence passed as body.

findings.claim: The TEMPLATE row stated the bare-hash rule unqualified.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a fence holding '####' and '#####' passes; the row's rule would read it empty.

findings.claim: The message offered 'close the fence' for a closed, intentional fence.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a draft quoting a never-written heading inside a correctly closed fence got '(close the fence, or write the section outside it)'.

findings.claim: The record arm's fence behaviour was claimed but pinned by no test.
findings.counterexample: Both DOCUMENT tests used an issue anchor with promptSource override; a direct probe confirmed the record behaviour, uncontrolled.

findings.claim: The empty-heading message disclosed nothing about the fenced-promised-heading rule.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: the F8 draft blocked with the bare 'has an empty heading'; a seat grepping the draft finds the heading with a line under it and cannot see why it read as empty.

findings.claim: The tilde-divider test pinned the opener line.
findings.counterexample: LATENT: it asserted only the message prefix; the hook reports 9 and the leg computed 9 independently.

findings.claim: The record row carried no fence note and the changeset said 'every Markdown renderer'.
findings.counterexample: Prose comparison against the changeset's own DOCUMENT paragraph; tilde fences are CommonMark/GFM, not original Markdown.pl.

findings.claim: The empty-heading suffix said 'its only content is X' and returned on the first rule.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a section with BOTH a #### line and a fenced promised heading printed only the fenced-heading reason; 'only' was false.

findings.claim: 'A section emptied by the new rules says which one … never a line the seat can see and not explain'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a section whose only content is an empty fence pair passed on main and blocked on HEAD with NO suffix; the emptying rule (a delimiter line is not body) is new in this PR.

findings.claim: A fenced line 'is body when non-blank unless it is a promised heading quoted verbatim'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a fence whose only line is '  ### Execution Flow' (indented, parenthetical dropped) is not body — promisedHeading trims and strips one parenthetical; the wiki mis-stated the fold's headline rule.

findings.claim: 'the cure the message gives is the right one: a bare closing fence'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED on ```mermaid closed by ```mermaid: the message said 'close it, or write the section outside it' — never 'bare', never the info string.

findings.claim: A closer with an info string does not close the fence (the class the MIGRATION documents).
findings.counterexample: LATENT: no fence test used a closer carrying text; deleting the rest.trim() guard left the suite green while the documented class inverted.

findings.claim: The never-closed cure fires only for the fence the copy sits in.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED and correct in code, but unpinned: no test had a copy in a closed fence beside an unrelated unclosed one, so weakening the guard passed all fence tests.

findings.claim: A fenced-only record 'is cured by editing the record, not by re-running totem spec'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: the hook's own BLOCKED line tells the seat to run totem spec --from <record>, which re-binds the same bytes and blocks again (a pre-existing tail).

findings.claim: promisedHeading extends 'the same tolerance the matcher extends'.
findings.counterexample: EXECUTED: a fenced '### Verification (of the sha256)' — a different heading sharing the stripped form — is not body; fail-closed, symmetric, undocumented.

findings.claim: 'a fence line indented four spaces is an indented code block'.
findings.counterexample: LATENT: after a paragraph the indented line is a lazy continuation under CommonMark 4.4, not an indented code block; reader behaviour identical.

verdict: Pass 1 (origin/main...1008f71e): the fix real and byte-parity clean, the fence state under-specified — four MATERIAL (fence length, an undisclosed false-block class, the DOCUMENT arm moved undisclosed, the wiki stale) and four MINOR, all folded. Pass 2 (8a4574ef): 13 CommonMark edges held; four MATERIAL (tolerant fenced heading as body, a vacuous pin, the info-string closer class, leading whitespace) and six MINOR, all folded. Pass 3 (74e21227): no behavioural defect, every probe unchanged or strictly more fail-closed; two MATERIAL prose residues and seven MINOR, folded in a wording-and-pins fold the leg is not re-armed on — convergence named.
